titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 22/2010 (ޖުޑިޝަރީގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Judicature Act (Act No. 22/2010). Clause 1 replaces Article 5 of that Act with new text split into several lettered sub-clauses, including time limits of 5 and 7 (the unit is hard to read and is probably days). It also changes a provision of the Judicial Service Commission Act (Act No. 13/2010, Article 26) to match. Clause 2 says the amendment takes effect once it is ratified and published in the Government Gazette. A table at the end sets the current text side by side with the proposed text. The scans are hard to read, so most details are uncertain.
whyItMatters: It changes rules in the law that organises the courts and in the law for the commission that oversees judges, but the scans do not make the practical effect clear.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 replaces Article 5 of the Judicature Act with new sub-clauses (a) onward. The wording of most of them could not be read reliably.
Several of the new sub-clauses refer to periods of 5 and 7, the unit of which is hard to read.
A further sub-clause changes how Article 26 of the Judicial Service Commission Act (Act No. 13/2010) applies, so the two laws line up.
Clause 2 says the amendment takes effect when it is ratified and published.
A comparison table at the end lists the existing wording against the proposed wording for each change.
whoIsAffected: Judges, the Judicial Service Commission and people who deal with the courts.
statedReasons: The explanatory note says the Judicature Act is being amended to change how the rules in Article 5 work together with the Judicial Service Commission Act. The scan is hard to read, so this is a rough reading.
